items.title: Read your Lambda concurrency quota in two Regions
items.kills: "Lambda scales without limit, in every Region the same."
items.read_only_alternative: This task is read-only. It needs no alternative.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Read the concurrency quota of your account in the current Region, and the part of it that no function reserves.
steps.expect: Two numbers, Quota and Unreserved. They are equal when no function in this Region reserves concurrency. A new account can show a lower Quota than the chapter: new accounts start with reduced quotas that AWS raises with usage.

steps.text: Run the same command for a second Region, <OTHER_REGION>. Choose a Region you do not work in, for example eu-west-1.
steps.expect: The two numbers of that Region. Compare them with step 1: each Region shows its own pair.

steps.text: List the default Lambda quotas of the current Region and read the Adjustable column.
steps.expect: A table of quota names, default values and True or False. True marks a quota you can ask to increase. False marks a quota you cannot change.

items.title: Stop a function with reserved concurrency zero and start it again
items.kills: "A function always scales to meet its requests."
items.cost: $0 for Lambda inside the free tier of one million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds per month: this task makes three short requests. Reserved concurrency incurs no additional charges, and IAM has no additional charge. CloudWatch Logs charges for the ingestion and storage of a few log lines.
items.cost_if_forgotten: $0 a day for the function and its role: you do not pay for idle capacity, and IAM has no additional charge. The log group keeps a few log lines, and CloudWatch Logs charges for their storage until you delete it.
items.read_only_alternative: In an account where you cannot create resources, read what is already there. aws lambda get-account-settings --query AccountLimit shows how much of the pool functions reserve: ConcurrentExecutions minus UnreservedConcurrentExecutions. aws lambda get-function-concurrency --function-name <FUNCTION_NAME> shows the reserved concurrency of one existing function. Neither command changes anything.

steps.text: Create a stack from a template that builds the routine part: an execution role that Lambda can assume, with the AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole policy, and a Python function named saa-lambda-t02 that returns a short answer.
steps.command: aws cloudformation create-stack --stack-name saa-lambda-t02 --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM --tags Key=book,Value=saa Key=task,Value=lambda-t02 --template-body '{"Resources":{"FnRole":{"Type":"AWS::IAM::Role","Properties":{"AssumeRolePolicyDocument":{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"lambda.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]},"ManagedPolicyArns":["arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole"]}},"Fn":{"Type":"AWS::Lambda::Function","Properties":{"FunctionName":"saa-lambda-t02","Runtime":"python3.13","Handler":"index.handler","Role":{"Fn::GetAtt":["FnRole","Arn"]},"Code":{"ZipFile":"def handler(event, context): return dict(ok=True)"}}}}}'

steps.text: Wait until AWS CloudFormation reports that the stack is complete.
steps.expect: No output when the stack is ready.

steps.text: Invoke the function synchronously. The CLI writes the answer of the function to the file response.json in your CloudShell home directory.
Set the reserved concurrency of the function to 0.
Invoke the function again, with the same command as in step 3.
steps.expect: After a short wait, an error that names TooManyRequestsException. No StatusCode 200.
steps.predict: The function worked a minute ago, and its code has not changed. What happens to this call?
steps.explain: A function stops processing events when you [set its reserved concurrency to 0](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-reserved-concurrency-zero-throttles), until you remove that limit. Each call then fails with a [throttling error (429 status code)](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-throttle-429). The AWS CLI and SDKs [automatically retry on client timeouts](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sdk-cli-auto-retry), throttling and service errors, so the error came after a short wait.

steps.text: Fix it: remove the reserved concurrency setting of the function.
Invoke the function a third time.

cleanup.text: Remove the reserved concurrency of the function, in case you stopped before step 6.
Delete the log group that Lambda created at the first invocation. Lambda made it outside the stack, so it has no book tag, and the stack does not delete it.
Delete the stack. AWS CloudFormation deletes the function and its role.
Wait until the stack is deleted.

verify.expect: An error that names ResourceNotFoundException: the function no longer exists. Then check the log group with aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix /aws/lambda/saa-lambda-t02 and expect an empty list.

still_costs: The log group /aws/lambda/saa-lambda-t02, if you skip its cleanup step: CloudWatch Logs charges for the storage of its log lines until you delete it.
Nothing else: an idle function and a reserved concurrency setting have no charge, and IAM has no additional charge.

items.title: Invoke a failing function both ways and find each error
items.kills: "Lambda retries every failed invocation and keeps the failed event."
items.cost: $0 for Lambda inside the free tier of one million requests and 400,000 GB-seconds per month: this task makes two short requests. IAM has no additional charge. The queue gets fewer than ten requests; its rates are on the Amazon SQS pricing page. CloudWatch Logs charges for the ingestion and storage of a few log lines.
items.cost_if_forgotten: $0 a day for the function and its role: you do not pay for idle capacity, and IAM has no additional charge. The queue keeps one message, and the Amazon SQS pricing page lists what a queue costs. CloudWatch Logs charges for the storage of a few log lines until you delete the log group.
items.read_only_alternative: In an account where you cannot create resources, read the asynchronous settings of an existing function: aws lambda list-function-event-invoke-configs --function-name <FUNCTION_NAME> shows MaximumRetryAttempts and DestinationConfig. An empty list means that nobody changed the retry settings and that the function has no destination. The command changes nothing.

steps.text: Create a standard queue that will receive the records of failed asynchronous calls.
steps.expect: No output: the shell keeps the queue URL in QUEUE_URL.

steps.text: Read the ARN of the queue. The role policy and the destination setting name the queue by this ARN.
steps.expect: No output: the shell keeps the queue ARN in QUEUE_ARN.

steps.text: Create a stack from a template for the routine part: an execution role that can send messages to this one queue, and a Python function named saa-lambda-t03 that raises an error on every call.
steps.command: aws cloudformation create-stack --stack-name saa-lambda-t03 --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM --parameters ParameterKey=QueueArn,ParameterValue=$QUEUE_ARN --tags Key=book,Value=saa Key=task,Value=lambda-t03 --template-body '{"Parameters":{"QueueArn":{"Type":"String"}},"Resources":{"FnRole":{"Type":"AWS::IAM::Role","Properties":{"AssumeRolePolicyDocument":{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"lambda.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]},"ManagedPolicyArns":["arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole"],"Policies":[{"PolicyName":"saa-send-to-failed-queue","PolicyDocument":{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":"sqs:SendMessage","Resource":{"Ref":"QueueArn"}}]}}]}},"Fn":{"Type":"AWS::Lambda::Function","Properties":{"FunctionName":"saa-lambda-t03","Runtime":"python3.13","Handler":"index.handler","Role":{"Fn::GetAtt":["FnRole","Arn"]},"Code":{"ZipFile":"def handler(event, context): raise RuntimeError(context.function_name)"}}}}}'

steps.text: Wait until AWS CloudFormation reports that the stack is complete.
steps.expect: No output when the stack is ready.

steps.text: Configure the asynchronous calls of the function: no retries, so that the test is quick, and an on-failure destination that sends a record to your queue.
steps.expect: MaximumRetryAttempts 0 and your queue ARN under OnFailure. If you see an error about permissions, wait one minute and run the command again.
StatusCode 200 and a FunctionError field, at once. The error details are in the file response.json.
steps.predict: The function fails, and it has an on-failure destination. Does Lambda retry this call, and does a record of it reach the queue?
steps.explain: For a synchronous call, the [status code is 200, even if the function returned an error](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sync-status-200-with-function-error). Lambda does not retry the call: the caller must [retry the invocation manually](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sync-error-caller-retries). The on-failure destination receives records of asynchronous invocations, here in [a standard SQS queue](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-async-destination-targets).

steps.text: Fix the test: invoke the same function asynchronously, with the invocation type Event.
steps.command: aws lambda invoke --function-name saa-lambda-t03 --invocation-type Event response.json
steps.expect: StatusCode 202 and no FunctionError field, although the function fails again.

steps.text: Read the bodies of the messages in the queue. The command waits for a message for 20 seconds.
steps.expect: One message, not two: the record of the asynchronous call. In requestContext, condition is RetriesExhausted and approximateInvokeCount is 1. If the list is empty, wait one minute and run the command again.

cleanup.text: Remove the asynchronous invocation settings of the function.
Delete the log group that Lambda created at the first invocation. Lambda made it outside the stack, so it has no book tag, and the stack does not delete it.
Delete the stack. AWS CloudFormation deletes the function and its role.
Wait until the stack is deleted.
Delete the queue and the message in it. If your CloudShell session ended, QUEUE_URL is empty: set it again to the URL that aws sqs get-queue-url --queue-name saa-lambda-t03-failed prints.

verify.expect: An error that says the queue does not exist. If it still prints the URL, wait one minute and run it again. Then check the log group with aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix /aws/lambda/saa-lambda-t03 and expect an empty list.

still_costs: The queue saa-lambda-t03-failed and its message, if you skip its cleanup step. The Amazon SQS pricing page lists what a queue costs.
The log group /aws/lambda/saa-lambda-t03, if you skip its cleanup step: CloudWatch Logs charges for the storage of its log lines until you delete it.
Nothing else: an idle function has no charge, and IAM has no additional charge.
